newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia troops clash on outskirts of capital.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia troops clash on outskirts of capital.

text.p: Rival Cambodian government troops clashed on the outskirts of Phnom Penh on Saturday, a military official loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said.
The clash was under way near a military base about 12 km (8 miles) northwest of the city, he said.

"The fighting is starting now. CPP troops have come to our base," said the military official inside the base, referring to troops loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP).
Witnesses in the area also reported hearing shooting but there were no reports of casualties.
The clash came as radio controlled by the CPP broadcast a warning from defence and security officials that searches were under way for "illegal troops" and weapons in the city.
Hun Sen warned earlier this week that Ranariddh's soldiers were bringing Khmer Rouge guerrilla defectors into the city illegally. Ranariddh has denied moving troops into the city.
Both prime ministers were out of the country on Saturday, their offices said.
The CPP radio broadcast a statement from defence and police officials saying officials would visit military facilities, hotels, schools and other civilian locations to search for illegal weapons.
Troops loyal to the feuding premiers fought a brief gun battle north of the city on Wednesday after a similar confrontation at an unofficial military checkpoint.
Political tension has been high in the capital since Hun Sen warned earlier this week he would use force if he found Ranariddh's military men bringing troops into Phnom Penh.
The two prime ministers head a divided coalition government after a long-running row over power-sharing and deep disagreement over policy towards the Khmer Rouge.
Analysts say the dispute over how to deal with the dwindling guerrilla movement reflected attempts by both men to bolster their positions ahead of elections next May.
The Khmer Rouge, responsible for the "killing fields" reign of terror in the 1970s, on Friday accused Hun Sen of plotting a coup against Ranariddh.
